subject: DPA redline: telemetry retention carveouts and escrow/rollback language
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-logistics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor Rhodes <connor.rhodes@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA — retention / telemetry redline questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Our legal team has a couple of requests we need clarified before we can proceed:

1) Retention windows: Section 4.2 currently states audit and telemetry logs may be retained up to 7 years. For regulatory reasons we need a maximum of 12 months for telemetry/operational logs and 3 years for security/audit logs unless otherwise required by law. Can Redwood carve telemetry (metrics/traces) separately from audit logs?

2) Onshore processing for EU-origin data: We operate in EMEA — we need an explicit commitment that EU customer data (including logs that could contain EU subject identifiers) remain within EU regions and are only processed in EU when requested.

3) Backup & escrow: The draft allows backups to be stored outside the region and retained under the same retention policy. For us, backups and escrow images that contain customer data must be covered by the same residency commitments or explicitly enumerated exceptions.

4) Evidence of deletion: We need a defined attestation process for confirmed erasure (Doc with dates, S3 delete markers, runbook reference). A lightweight certificate in operational format would be fine.

I've attached our redline of the DPA (ACME_DPA_redline_v3.docx) with inline suggestions. Can you confirm which items Redwood can accept and which need alternative language?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement timeline is tight.

Best,
Lina

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — retention / telemetry redline questions

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear redlines and timeline. Looping in Marcus (legal) and Ben (account lead) so we can respond to each point and propose operational artifacts.

Quick summary of what we can do immediately:
- Telemetry vs audit: We can separate telemetry (metrics, traces, debug logs) from audit/security logs and offer a 12-month default for telemetry with the option to shorten to 30 days as a tiered configuration for ultra-sensitive customers.
- Evidence of deletion: We can provide an erasure attestation packet (runbook reference, timestamped manifest, and storage delete markers) and can include a simple template certificate in the DPA appendix.

Open items for agreement:
- Backups/escrow: We need to confirm scope. Our standard backup copying/replication for disaster recovery may cross regions; providing onshore-only backups for EMEA requires an ops change and a contractual commitment. Marcus — can legal outline what we can contractually guarantee vs. an operational amendment?

Next steps: Marcus to propose legal language for backup/escrow residency exceptions and Ben to propose a commercial concession if we need to invest in region-specific backups.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a short follow-up call if helpful.

— Priya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Redwood DPA — retention / telemetry redline questions

Priya / Ben / Lina — thanks, Lina, for the redline. Below are suggested edits and rationale; I’ve tried to keep the language operationally accurate while minimizing exposure.

1) Telemetry v. Audit retention (Section 4.2):
Suggested wording: "Telemetry (operational metrics, traces, non-identifiable debug metrics) shall be retained no longer than twelve (12) months. Audit logs and security-relevant logs (authentication events, access logs, audit trails) shall be retained for a period not to exceed thirty-six (36) months, unless required by applicable law."
Rationale: Keeps the two buckets separate and gives Acme the 12/36 split they requested. We will need to document how we classify logs (appendix).

2) Onshore processing / Residency (Section 3.1):
Suggested wording: "Customer Data originating in the European Economic Area (EEA) will, at Customer's request, be stored and processed in EEA region-only infrastructure where commercially reasonable. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure backups and replicas for such Customer Data are also stored within the EEA; however, Redwood may utilize cross-region disaster recovery capabilities where required for system continuity."
Rationale: This is a compromise — we accept EU-only processing 'at Customer's request' with a 'commercially reasonable efforts' qualifier for backups/replicas. If Acme requires contractually binding onshore-only backups, that should be a premium commitment.

3) Backups & escrow images (new subsection):
Suggested wording: "For the avoidance of doubt, backups, snapshots, and escrow images containing Customer Data are subject to the residency commitments set forth in Section 3.1, provided that Customer and Redwood mutually agree to any operational changes and associated fees necessary to implement region-specific backup retention."
Rationale: Creates a path to say yes, but with an operational/price trigger.

4) Erasure attestation (Appendix B):
We can commit to providing a deletion certificate that includes deletion timestamps, object keys, and runbook references within thirty (30) days of a valid erasure request.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Redwood DPA — retention / telemetry redline questions

Quick commercial note for context — if Acme wants firm contractual language that forces all backups/escrow artifacts to be stored onshore for EEA-origin data (no exceptions), that will require us to commit engineering time and an ongoing operational margin. Typical options we offer:

A) Standard commitment (no additional fee): residency-by-request for live data and best-effort for backups (Marcus language).
B) Premium commitment (one-time onboarding fee + 12-month uplift): guaranteed region-restricted backups and escrow images; Redwood will maintain region-only replica buckets for Acme account.

If Acme signals B, we can draft a short SOW and present an estimated engineering lead time (6-10w) and a recurring cost.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-logistics.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Jun 2028 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA — retention / telemetry redline questions

Thanks everyone — the proposed language is helpful and we appreciate the pragmatic approach. A few follow-ups before we finalize:

• The 12/36 split for telemetry/audit looks acceptable; please add the appendix that defines "telemetry" vs "audit" fields.
• For the residency/backups: Acme will initially accept the "commercially reasonable efforts" language for backups, provided Redwood includes the premium SOW as an optional addendum that we can activate within 90 days if we see any noncompliance. That addendum should include an estimated cost and lead time.
• Erasure attestation: please confirm the format of the certificate (PDF with manifest + timestamped object keys is fine) and that the 30-day delivery window is acceptable.

If you can post a clean DPA with Marcus' suggested edits and the optional SOW draft by EOD Monday, we can move this to procurement signature next week.

Best regards,
Lina
